value.name: Cervical Spondylosis
value.description: Cervical spondylosis is a general term for age-related wear and tear affecting the spinal disks in your neck. As the disks dehydrate and shrink, signs of bone-on-bone contact appear, leading to bone spurs and other changes in the bones and ligaments that support the spine. It is a common condition, especially as people age.
symptoms: Headaches, often starting in the back of the head
Pain that worsens with coughing or sneezing
Reduced ability to turn the head
Numbness or weakness in arms, hands, or legs

value.name: Herniated Cervical Disc
value.description: A herniated cervical disc occurs when the soft, gel-like center of a spinal disc in the neck pushes out through a tear in the tougher exterior. This can put pressure on the spinal cord or nearby nerves, causing pain and other symptoms. It is often caused by wear and tear or sudden injury.
symptoms: Neck pain that may radiate to the shoulder and arm
Numbness or tingling in the arm or hand
Muscle weakness in the arm or hand
Pain that worsens with certain movements

value.name: Neck Strain
value.description: A neck strain, also known as a stiff neck, is a common condition caused by overstretching or tearing of muscles or tendons in the neck. It often results from poor posture, sleeping in an awkward position, or sudden movements. The pain can range from mild to severe and often limits neck movement.
symptoms: Limited range of motion in the neck

value.name: Meningitis
value.description: Meningitis is an inflammation of the membranes (meninges) surrounding the brain and spinal cord. It can be caused by viral, bacterial, or fungal infections. Bacterial meningitis is particularly serious and can be life-threatening if not treated promptly.

value.name: Thyroid Nodules
value.description: Thyroid nodules are lumps that form within the thyroid gland, a small gland located at the base of the neck. Most thyroid nodules are benign (noncancerous), but some can be cancerous. They often cause no symptoms and are discovered incidentally during medical examinations.
symptoms: A lump or swelling in the neck
Pain in the neck, jaw, or ears
